newsitem.title: USA: Ariz Glen Canyon hydropower dam flows cut slightly.
newsitem.headline: Ariz Glen Canyon hydropower dam flows cut slightly.

text.p: Flows through the Glen Canyon dam in Arizona will be reduced from Tuesday in line with a lower estimate for spring runoff on the Colorado River, a spokesman for the U.S. Bureau of Reclamation (BuRec) said Monday.
The hydroelectric project has been running at much higher than normal rates since mid-January to make space in the dam's reservoir for water from the spring runoff.
Glen Canyon has a power generating capacity of 1,356 megawatts.
The early March estimate for snowpack along the Colorado River basin was reduced to 162 percent of normal, compared with an early-February forecast of 171 percent of normal, the BuRec spokesman said.
The dam is now running at a rate of 27,000 cubic feet per second (cfs), but that will drop to 24,000 cfs on Tuesday and to 21,000 cfs on May 1.
"We are still way above normal operating rates and will remain there until the end of April," the spokesman noted.
"By the end of July, the reservoir will be close to full and the runoff will be over," he added.
